specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** read-a-greek-sign
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** use
**Learning Objective:** The learner will use the Greek letter table to transliterate twelve Greek signs from our route into Latin letters, with at least 10 of 12 correct within two attempts each. **Prerequisites:** alphabet, Greek language, the Greek capital letters and their sign transliterations, the letter pairs ΟΥ, ΑΙ, ΕΙ, ΟΙ (all defined in the section "The Greek Language" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each sign, the learner types a transliteration in Latin letters. An answer is correct when, after the normalization in Rules, it matches one of the Accepted answers in Content. Mastery is 10 of 12 signs correct within two attempts. Viewing the letter key is support, not evidence; the typed answer is the evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Η is the consonant h (it is the vowel i). (2) Ρ is p (it is r). (3) Χ is x (it is a throaty h, written ch). (4) Υ is u (alone it is y, sounding ee). (5) Ω is w (it is o). (6) Λ is an upside-down v (it is l). (7) Greek signs must be read letter by letter for pronunciation (pairs like ΕΙ and ΟΥ make one sound). **Instructional Rationale:** Transliteration is an Apply-level procedure: the learner must use the letter table on new words. Typing the answer rather than choosing it forces the learner to map every letter, and the per-sign trap letters make each misconception surface where it is most likely. **Content:** The full letter table from the chapter section "The Greek Language" (24 capitals with their sign transliteration) is available from a "Letter key" button at all times. Signs, in this fixed order: | # | Sign shown | Accepted answers | Meaning | Sounds like | Trap letters (named in feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | ΑΘΗΝΑ | athina | Athens | a-THEE-na | Θ is th; Η is i, not h | | 2 | ΠΕΙΡΑΙΑΣ | peiraias; pireas | Piraeus, the port of Athens | pee-reh-AHS | Ρ is r, not p | | 3 | ΡΟΔΟΣ | rodos | Rhodes | RO-thos | Ρ is r; Δ is d, sounding like th in this | | 4 | ΗΡΑΚΛΕΙΟ | irakleio; iraklio | Heraklion | ee-RA-klee-o | Η is i; Λ is l | | 5 | ΚΝΩΣΟΣ | knosos; knossos | Knossos | kno-SOS | Ω is o, not w | | 6 | ΔΕΛΦΟΙ | delfoi; delfi; delphi | Delphi | del-FEE | Λ is l; Φ is f | | 7 | ΑΚΡΟΠΟΛΗ | akropoli | Acropolis | a-KRO-po-lee | Ρ is r; Η is i | | 8 | ΜΟΥΣΕΙΟ | mouseio; mousio | Museum | moo-SEE-o | ΟΥ is ou, sounding oo | | 9 | ΕΙΣΟΔΟΣ | eisodos; isodos | Entrance | EE-so-thos | ΕΙ sounds ee; Σ is s | | 10 | ΕΞΟΔΟΣ | exodos; eksodos | Exit | EX-o-thos | Ξ is x, sounding ks | | 11 | ΚΛΕΙΣΤΟ | kleisto; klisto | Closed | klee-STO | Λ is l; ΕΙ sounds ee | | 12 | ΑΝΟΙΧΤΟ | anoichto; anichto; anihto | Open | a-nee-KHTO | Χ is ch, not x; ΟΙ sounds ee | **Provenance:** Sign words are standard Modern Greek. Transliterations follow the ELOT 743 standard used on Greek road and site signs (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanization_of_Greek), with common informal spellings added as accepted answers. Meanings and pronunciations are from the chapter section "The Greek Language"; the generator must check each pronunciation's stressed syllable against the word's Wiktionary entry and keep it only if it matches. **Rules:** Normalize the learner's answer by converting to lowercase and removing spaces, hyphens and accent marks before comparing. An answer is correct if the normalized text equals any accepted answer for that sign. No partial credit. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees sign 1 in capitals, styled as a sign, with a text box and a Letter key button. 2. The learner types a transliteration and submits it. 3. If correct, the meaning and pronunciation appear, and the learner moves on. 4. If wrong on the first attempt, the trap-letter note appears and the learner tries again. If wrong on the second attempt, the sign is shown letter by letter with each Greek letter above its Latin letter, then the meaning and pronunciation, and the sign counts as missed. 5. After all twelve signs, the learner sees a summary of all twelve with meanings, and the letters they missed most often. 6. The learner should notice that most of the letters are the same as ours, and that a handful of look-alikes (Η, Ρ, Χ, Υ) cause most mistakes. **Feedback:** Twelve signs in fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: is , '', sounding like ." First incorrect: "Not yet. Watch the trap letters: ." Second incorrect: the letter-by-letter breakdown plus "This sign says : ." A running score "Signs read: n of 12" is shown. At the end: "10 or more: you can read Greek signs" or "Fewer than 10: review the letter table and try again." A Restart button clears all answers. **Starting State:** Sign 1, ΑΘΗΝΑ, with an empty answer box and the prompt "Sound it out: what does this sign say?" **Chapter Anchors:** 24 Greek capital letters. ΠΕΙΡΑΙΑΣ reads "Peiraias," sounding pee-reh-AHS. ΚΛΕΙΣΤΟ reads "Kleisto," klee-STO, "closed." ΑΝΟΙΧΤΟ, a-nee-KHTO, "open." ΔΕΛΦΟΙ appears as "Delfoi" and sounds like del-FEE. Twelve signs.
